lines.trans: Excuse me, Javier? Sorry to disturb you.
Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was just looking for it.
You left it beside the soup cup on the front counter.
All my street notes from this week are in here. You saved me.
We are glad our courtyard is peaceful for your... work.
Very peaceful! Though did you just hear a strange metallic knock?
Yes! It sounded as if it came from the heating pipe in the corner.

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: Touch the radiator: the top is lukewarm, yet the bottom is getting cold.
Oh! Sometimes old pipes have an air bubble at night.
I have a warm blanket, so tonight I am very comfortable.
Thank you for being so patient! Mateo will check the cellar right away.
Good night, Clara. See you at breakfast.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Indicates position or movement downward.

examples.trans: The kitchen is downstairs.

examples.text: Te espero abajo en el patio.
examples.trans: I will wait for you downstairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Describes clothing, blankets, or rooms that keep out the cold.

examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Tengo una manta abrigada, así que esta noche estoy muy cómodo.
examples.trans: I have a warm blanket, so tonight I am very comfortable.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!
Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Al aire libre means 'outdoors'.

examples.text: El aire es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The air is very important here.
We talk about the air.

alegrar.gloss: to make glad; to cheer up

meanings.en: to make glad; to cheer up
meanings.note: Me alegra / nos alegra means 'it makes me/us glad'.

examples.trans: That news makes us very glad.

examples.text: Las flores alegran toda la mesa.
examples.trans: The flowers brighten up the whole table.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.
It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Takes indicative for known facts and subjunctive for hypotheticals.

examples.trans: We are going out even though it is raining a bit.

examples.text: Esperaré aquí aunque tarde diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will wait here even if he takes ten minutes.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Air or water bubble.

examples.trans: The bubble is here.

examples.text: Vemos las burbujas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bubbles from the door.

buscar.gloss: to look for; to search for

meanings.en: to look for; to search for
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'for' (busco la llave = I am looking for the key).

examples.trans: I am looking for the blue door.

examples.text: Ayer busqué mis gafas por toda la casa.
examples.trans: Yesterday I looked for my glasses all over the house.

meanings.note: Central heating system.

examples.text: La calefacción es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The heating is very important here.
We talk about the heating.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Bound paper notebook.

examples.trans: The notebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuadernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notebooks from the door.

meanings.note: De cuero = made of leather.

examples.text: El cuero es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The leather is very important here.
We talk about the leather.

meanings.note: Always carries a written accent on the first syllable.

examples.trans: It is a comfortable piece.

examples.text: Tengo una manta abrigada, así que esta noche estoy muy cómodo.
examples.trans: I have a warm blanket, so tonight I am very comfortable.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Takes an accent in present boot forms: se enfría.

examples.text: El bizcocho se enfría en la rejilla.
examples.trans: The cake cools on the wire rack.

examples.text: Bebe el té antes de que se enfríe.
examples.trans: Drink your tea before it gets cold.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: De golpe = all of a sudden.

examples.trans: The knock is here.

examples.text: Vemos los golpes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the knocks from the door.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.trans: Sit next to the window.
We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Warm wool or cotton bed blanket.

examples.trans: The blanket is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the blankets from the door.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: La persiana metálica = the metal shop shutter.

examples.trans: It is a metal piece.
Good! Is the metal shutter open?

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Siento molestarle = sorry to bother you.

examples.trans: Excuse me, am I bothering you for a second?

examples.text: Aquí el ruido de los coches no molesta.
examples.trans: Here car noise does not bother anyone.

meanings.note: Reception desk or shop counter.

examples.trans: The counter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mostradores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the counters from the door.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!
The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Tener paciencia = to be patient.

examples.text: La paciencia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The patience is very important here.
We talk about the patience.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Core contrast conjunction.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera, pero dentro se está bien.
examples.trans: It is cold outside, yet inside it is cosy.

examples.text: Es pequeño, pero tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: It is small, but it has lots of light.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Hot-water room radiator.

examples.trans: The radiator is here.

examples.text: Vemos los radiadores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the radiators from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Qué raro! = How strange!

examples.trans: It is a strange piece.

examples.text: ¡Muy tranquilo! Aunque, ¿acaba de oír un golpe metálico raro?
examples.trans: Very peaceful! Though did you just hear a strange metallic knock?

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El vecino revisa los radiadores en otoño.
examples.trans: El vecino checks the radiators in autumn.

examples.text: Revisamos dos veces la lista de reservas.
examples.trans: We double-checked the booking list.

meanings.note: ¡Salvados! = Saved!

examples.trans: It is a saved piece.

examples.text: Aquí están todas mis notas de la calle de esta semana. Me ha salvado.
examples.trans: All my street notes from this week are in here. You saved me.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.trans: The week is here.

examples.text: Vemos las semanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the weeks from the door.

sentir.gloss: to feel; to be sorry (lo siento)

meanings.en: to feel; to be sorry (lo siento)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie in present, e -> i in preterite 3rd: sintió).

examples.text: Lo siento mucho por la espera.
examples.trans: I am very sorry about the wait.

examples.text: Aquí cada huésped se siente en casa.
examples.trans: Here every guest feels at home.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Hecho una sopa = soaked through.

examples.trans: The soup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sopas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soups from the door.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Brick basement beneath a building.

examples.trans: The cellar is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sótanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cellars from the door.

meanings.note: After a verb, invariable tanto means 'so much' (¿por qué mira tanto?).

examples.text: ¿Cómo recuerdas eso después de tantos años?
examples.trans: How do you remember that after so many years?
Thank you for having so much patience.

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

meanings.note: Pleasantly warm (not scalding hot).

examples.trans: It is a warm piece.

examples.text: Toque el radiador: arriba está templado, pero abajo se está enfriando.
examples.trans: Touch the radiator: the top is lukewarm, yet the bottom is getting cold.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Dos toques cortos = two short rings.

examples.trans: The ring is here.

examples.text: Vemos los toques desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rings from the door.

meanings.note: Ir al trabajo = go to work.

examples.trans: The work is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trabajos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the works from the door.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Water or heating pipe.

examples.trans: The pipe is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tuberías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pipes from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

venir.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.en: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)
meanings.note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene, vine.

examples.trans: Thank you for coming this morning.

examples.text: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
examples.trans: See you next week.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!
